text:
sarah: Heads up — during the 0200 batch window eu-west-1 we had ~6 GPU nodes in nodepool 'gpu-timeslice-eu' repeatedly go NotReady and pods evicted. Notmemory/OOMs — kubelet logs show repeated gRPC disconnects to the NVIDIA driver stack and a bunch of NVLink errors.

alex: ugh. anything obvious in node-exporter / tcptrace?

sarah: spikes on the node's ENI TX queue, and pod networking counters show retransmits. but packet loss doesn't match host NIC failure patterns. also saw cluster-autoscaler scale-up delays ~3m because it considered time-sliced GPUs "sufficient" due to fractional alloc.

mike: hmm looks like two separate things colliding: (1) time-sliced GPU sharing creates lots of small attach/detach and kernel context switches, (2) high cross-zone control plane traffic for autoscaler decisions + KMS calls = transient throttles. combined they push the GPU infra over the edge.

jess: are we sure it's time-slicing (MIG / vendor timeslice) and not just too many pods per GPU? what's the current MIG profile mix?

sarah: mix is 1xA100-4g + 2xA100-2g typical (MIG-like partitions), and we also enable a gvisor sidecar on batch jobs which adds more ephemeral connections. pods-per-gpu at peak = ~18.

alex: can we repro in staging with a synthetic workload that pulses small inference jobs + KMS rotations? would help isolate NIC vs kernel xfault.

mike: agree. short-term mitigation: separate nodepool for time-sliced workloads behind a taint so autoscaler doesn't count them for low-latency pools. longer-term: add a custom metric for effective GPU availability so cluster-autoscaler sees real allocable capacity.

jess: proposed quick commands to isolate:
```bash
# taint the timeslice pool so only tolerant jobs land there
kubectl taint nodes -l nodepool=gpu-timeslice-eu gpu-timeslice=true:NoSchedule

# nodepool for dedicated low-latency queries
# create with label nodepool=gpu-dedicated-eu, no MIG slicing
```

alex: and autoscaler config snippet to ignore that pool for scale-to-zero decisions:
```yaml
clusterAutoscaler:
  skipNodesWithLocalStorage: false
  expander: least-waste
  nodeGroups:
    - name: gpu-dedicated-eu
      minSize: 2
      maxSize: 50
    - name: gpu-timeslice-eu
      minSize: 2
      maxSize: 200
      scaleDownDisabled: true # avoid churn during batch windows
```

sarah: cost note: time-slicing = higher utilization but increased tail failures and operator toil. running dedicated full-GPUs for qps-sensitive routes increased infra $/token but reduced incident MTTR. we need to model OPEX vs downtime cost.

mike: can we also throttle KMS calls and push caching to avoid hitting control-plane quotas? saw spikes in KMS for ephemeral creds during batch start.

jess: yes, add local credential cache and extend key TTL for batch jobs. also recommend increasing ENI queue sizes and bumping NIC IRQ affinity for those nodepools.

infra-bot: incident-created #inc-2026 linked -> summary: eu-west-1 GPU node flaps during batch window, suspected interaction between MIG/time-slice workloads and control plane throttling.

alex: concrete action items: 1) run repro in staging with synthetic requests and KMS load (mike + sarah), 2) spin up dedicated nodepool for low-latency traffic + taint (jess), 3) add custom metric 'gpu_alloc_success_rate' for autoscaler (alex), 4) implement KMS caching & ENI tuning (mike).

sarah: I'll own step 1 and collect packet captures + dmesg. putting a small canary in prod: create 'gpu-dedicated-eu' with 2 nodes and route 5% qps there for an hour, see if tail latency improves.

mike: +1. also let's add a postmortem template item to capture MIG profile fragmentation details (how many partial GPUs left unused when pods fail).

jess: ping me once canary is up — I'll watch NIC metrics and kubelet logs.

sarah: thanks all — will post results in this thread. :thumbsup:
